frontend.tech: Elm 0.19.1 browser app via Lamdera frontend runtime (elm/browser + elm/html virtual DOM)

backend.tech: Elm 0.19.1 server-side app via Lamdera backend runtime (lamdera/core + lamdera/codecs), single shared in-memory game model broadcast to clients

database.tech: None in this repo. State lives only in the in-memory Lamdera backend model; the only persistence-related artifacts are compiler-generated Evergreen state snapshots/migrations consumed by the Lamdera platform, not a local database

external.name: Lamdera platform (hosting, auto-deploy via git remote, Evergreen state storage across redeploys)
elm-explorations/test (unit test framework, run by elm-test in CI)

db.notes: There is NO database in this repo: treat the versioned serialized state as the 'data layer'. src/Evergreen/ holds compiler-generated state snapshots (V1/V3/V5/V10) and migrations between them (the 'schema evolution' to model); src/Types/ + src/Types.elm hold the current state shape (Game record, Tile/Meeple/Feature, FrontendModel/BackendModel and message types). tests/ pin expected state behavior. Scope = 39 files, ~1,600 lines.

classes.notes: Elm has no classes: model the records, custom types and module boundaries instead. Cover all of src/ plus tests/ (48 files, ~3,820 lines). Treat src/Evergreen/ as generated snapshots mirroring current types (see `src/Evergreen/Migrate/V10.elm:3`), not as hand-designed types; review/ is a separate elm-review tooling project, out of scope.

flows.notes: Trace the message flow: view click -> FrontendMsg -> update -> sendToBackend ToBackend -> Backend.updateFromFrontend -> broadcast ToFrontend -> Frontend.updateFromBackend -> new view. Key async re-entries are the Random Cmds: Random.generate InitializeGameAndTileDrawStackShuffled and TileDrawStackShuffled (draw-stack refills after each turn). Note src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm is imported BY the backend (client-side validation shared with server), not frontend-only. 11 files, ~2,530 lines.

usecases.notes: The actor is the browser player. Entry points are view clicks (Register `src/Views/PlayerRegistrationView.elm:26`, start game `src/Views/PlayerLobbyView.elm:21`, board click `src/Views/GameView.elm:327`, meeple click `src/Views/GameView.elm:533`) -> Frontend.elm update -> ToBackend messages -> Backend.updateFromFrontend handlers. Backend state gates everything: BePlayerRegistration (lobby) vs BeGamePlayed (game) (`src/Types.elm:11-17`). 8 files, ~1,440 lines.

domain.notes: Domain model: Tile (4 sides each with SideId + Feature, optional cloister, rotation `src/Types/Tile.elm:1`), Meeple (SideId owner `src/Types/Meeple.elm:1`), Game (TileGrid, Meeples, PlayerScores, draw stack, turn state `src/Types/Game.elm:28-40`), GameState PlaceTile/PlaceMeeple/Finished (`src/Types/GameState.elm:4-7`). Game rules (rotation, SideId merging on placement, majority scoring, 2x city bonus, cloister completion) live in src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm; the 74-tile tileset is hand-written data in src/Helpers/TileMapper.elm; tests/ pin expected behavior. 14 files, ~1,515 lines.

top_processes.name: Player registration and lobby join
top_processes.why: Entry point of the whole app: name validation client-side, server-side duplicate/lobby-full checks (limit 5), broadcast of updated player list to all clients

top_processes.name: Lobby management (kick player / kill lobby)
top_processes.why: Lobby-only side flow: KickPlayer and KillLobby mutate the registration state and broadcast PlayerKicked/LobbyKilled, forcing kicked clients back to the registration screen (`src/Frontend.elm:98-124`)

top_processes.name: Game initialization with shuffled tile draw
top_processes.why: Lobby-to-game transition: initializeGame builds the 74-tile draw stack and starting grid, Random.generate shuffles it, and getPlayableTileFromDrawstack skips unplaceable tiles for the first draw

top_processes.name: Placing a tile on the board (turn step 1)
top_processes.why: Core turn loop: placeTile inserts the tile and merges SideIds of adjacent features across the grid and meeple dict, then switches GameState to PlaceMeepleState; placement validity is only checked client-side (`src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:48-110`)

top_processes.name: Rotating the drawn tile
top_processes.why: Pre-placement interaction: rotateLeft permutes the four sides and isRotatedCorrectly cross-checks against the canonical tile from the tileset

top_processes.name: Placing a meeple with immediate feature scoring
top_processes.why: Turn step 2 and the most complex flow: places meeple (or skips), scores every newly finished feature by majority with a 2x bonus for completed cities, returns finished meeples, advances the turn, and re-shuffles the draw stack via Random.generate

top_processes.name: End-of-game final scoring
top_processes.why: When the draw stack yields no playable tile, finishGame scores all remaining features and cloisters, empties the meeple dict and sets FinishedState, determining the winner

top_processes.name: Rejoining an in-progress game
top_processes.why: A player registering while BeGamePlayed is active receives JoinedGame{game} and re-enters FeGamePlayed; the readme advertises this reconnection for disconnected players (`readme.md:123`)

risks.risk: No local database or persistence layer: the entire game (players, grid, scores) lives in the in-memory Lamdera backend model, so a server restart with no Evergreen snapshot loses the game; any 'DB analyst' work here is about the serialized state snapshots, not a datastore
risks.citation: `src/Backend.elm:14-15` (Model = single BackendModel), `src/Evergreen/Migrate/V10.elm:3-18` (snapshots managed by the Lamdera platform, not a local DB)

risks.risk: Legacy versioned state: four parallel copies of the core types (Evergreen V1/V3/V5/V10) mirror the current src/Types, and the V10 migration does ModelReset for both frontend and backend models, discarding previously persisted state at that boundary - analysts must not treat V1-V10 as live code paths

Compiler-generated code inside src/: Evergreen migration files are auto-generated by the Lamdera compiler (and the Evergreen/V*/Types.* snapshots mirror current types), so they document state evolution but must not be modeled as hand-written design or logic
risks.citation: `src/Evergreen/Migrate/V10.elm:3` ('This migration file was automatically generated by the lamdera compiler'), `src/Evergreen/Migrate/V5.elm:3`

risks.risk: Debug code in the backend hot path: Debug.log runs on every client connection in production code

Client-trusted rules: placeTile and placeMeeple explicitly 'do not check whether the move is valid'; placement validity is only enforced client-side in FrontendHelpers, so a tampered client could place invalid tiles or meeples (no server-side turn/validity enforcement)
risks.citation: `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:311-314` and `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:373-376` ('Does not check whether the move is valid'), `src/Helpers/FrontendHelpers.elm:48-110`

risks.risk: Thin test coverage: only 2 test files (296 lines) against ~3,524 lines of src; CI does run elm-test plus elm-review and compiles both entry points

Spec mismatch - field scoring: the readme documents end-of-game field scoring (3 points per adjacent completed city) but finishGame only counts generic feature tile counts and cloisters, with no field-specific rule; fields instead score by raw tile count
risks.citation: `readme.md:79`, `src/Helpers/GameLogic.elm:511-556` (finishGame has no Field case; Feature enum has Field at `src/Types/Feature.elm:7`)

risks.risk: Spec mismatch - meeple economy: the readme says 6 meeples + 1 score-track meeple per player, but the code gives a flat 7 meeples and implements no score track
